name: Endpoint and Workload Protection Coverage Report
description: Coverage and health of protective software across endpoints and servers in scope, reconciled to the authoritative asset inventory rather than to the protection tool's own device list.

expected_content.element: List of devices and workloads with protective software installed, with last check-in time
expected_content.why: Installation without recent check-in is functionally the same as absence.

expected_content.element: Authoritative asset inventory for the same date, with reconciliation against the protected list
expected_content.why: A tool cannot report on assets it never enrolled, so its own list always looks complete.

expected_content.element: Agent health and definition or signature currency where applicable
expected_content.why: A stale agent evidences deployment, not protection.

expected_content.element: Coverage measured across the period rather than at a single date
expected_content.why: Coverage degrades as assets are added; a point-in-time figure hides that.

expected_content.element: Explicit treatment of contractor and personally owned devices, or a statement that they are outside the boundary
expected_content.why: Silence here is the most common coverage ambiguity.

expected_content.element: Where workloads are immutable and ephemeral, image provenance and integrity verification instead of resident agents
expected_content.why: For containerised workloads this is usually the stronger control, and applying an endpoint model to them produces a false gap.

owner: IT Operations, with Security Engineering accountable for the standard
source_system_examples: Endpoint detection and response console coverage report
Container image scanning and signing pipeline records

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default of one monthly cadence plus a 15-day grace window. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Device names frequently identify individuals; tokenise where reconciliation to the inventory is preserved.
Do not include detection detail or threat artifacts in a coverage report.
retention_guidance: Retain monthly coverage snapshots across the period so degradation over time is visible.

validation_rules.rule: A coverage report exists for each in-scope asset class.
Protected devices reconcile to the authoritative asset inventory for the same date.
Agent health and check-in currency are reported, not installation alone.
Coverage is evidenced across the period rather than at a single date.
The protection approach matches the workload type; resident agents are not expected on immutable ephemeral workloads.
The report is exported from the management console rather than compiled manually.

common_issues.issue: Coverage reported as a percentage of the tool's own enrolled devices.
common_issues.impact: Always approaches 100% and says nothing about unenrolled assets.

common_issues.issue: Agents installed but not checking in for months.
common_issues.impact: Deployment is evidenced; protection is not.

common_issues.issue: Contractor devices neither covered nor declared out of boundary.
common_issues.impact: Coverage of the in-scope population cannot be concluded either way.

common_issues.issue: Endpoint agent expectations applied to ephemeral container workloads.
common_issues.impact: Produces a false gap where image integrity is the appropriate control.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: DriftGuard names no product category as required. Where an entity meets the objective through immutable infrastructure and verified images, the absence of a resident agent is not a deficiency.
